Water Master Plan Tool

Welcome to this limited version of WSC's fully functional mock-up. The purpose of this tool is to walk through some of the functionality that WSC can build into PCWA's production toolset, which can allow staff to track demand, time the next expansion, and keep CIP costs current.

Open the Plan Overview

Potential Deliverables

WSC has the ability to build varying levels of tools that are designed to provide PCWA the most value while right-sizing deliverables to work within PCWA's technical ecosystem. Deliverables can range from a single self-contained HTML file that runs in your browser to installable programs that can directly interface with other products in your ecosystem.

For all but the most limited deliverable options, PCWA staff will be able to load direct exports from third-party tools via the Update tab simulated here. This includes demands, triggers, project costs, bid tabs, and CIP updates, with every accepted change recorded under the name of the person who loaded it and the date.

Getting Around

  • The screens on the left follow the order most readers use, from the Plan Overview through to the annual Update, and you can jump to any of them at any time.
  • The growth case, horizon, and cost year switches near the top of a screen change every figure on that screen, so you can compare cases without leaving the page.
  • The Guide button in the top bar opens the user guide at the screen you are viewing, and Tours walks you through the larger workflows step by step.
  • Edit unlocks changes with the editor password, and the gear in the top bar opens the settings that control how the plan behaves.

The screens, in the order most readers use them

  1. 1. Plan OverviewThe figures at a glance, followed by the projects that need action or attention and where they are.
  2. 2. DemandAverage and maximum day demand by zone, with the year each capacity step will be needed.
  3. 3. MapMains by diameter, with each 5-year project main and its record.
  4. 4. ProjectsThe CIP by fiscal year against the fund target, with the candidate projects.
  5. 5. CostsUnit costs from bids, markups, escalation, and re-priced projects.
  6. 6. UpdateThe yearly checklist that loads new data and records each change.
This mock-up uses invented figures so that the workflow can be shown without any PCWA records. No number in this file comes from agency data.

How build-out is built

Every parcel carries its adopted land use and a unit demand factor from the agency's own meter data. Build-out is the sum. The growth case only phases that total in time, so build-out stays separate from the growth assumption. A new land use layer re-runs the sum; the unit factors change only in a master plan update.

Map

The map colors every water main by diameter and highlights the mains that belong to the 5-year projects in orange. Clicking a main's tag opens its record and its projects in the panel beside the map, which is one way a production tool can connect the CIP back to the GIS.

8 in. and smaller10 to 12 in.14 to 16 in.18 to 24 in.over 24 in.

How unit costs are built

Each standard item takes one price from the agency's bids by a stated rule. Items roll up into assemblies, such as the cost per foot of a 12-inch main in a collector street with its trench, paving, valves and services. Each project is its quantity times its assembly, plus contingency by estimate class and the soft costs. A new bid changes every project that uses the items it priced.

How bid tabs become unit costs

Each bid is imported once. Every bid line is matched to a standard item, such as an 8-inch open-cut PVC main with concrete encasement, and the match is remembered for that bidder. Costs that are not per foot, such as mobilization, valves and design, are spread into the cost per foot of main. Prices are brought to the cost year, then combined across bids by a stated rule. The spread of prices is kept, so the reader can see how firm each unit cost is.

Import

Import a bid tab after each bid, or batch the year's bids at once. A new layout needs a one-time column setup, which the wizard saves per bidder.

Update

This screen walks staff through the annual update as a checklist, where each step loads one export, checks it against its template, and lists the proposed changes for acceptance, so that the plan stays current without any retyping.

Annual update checklist Level 2 option

Work down the list once a year, or when a new bid or a new land use plan arrives. Each step says what to load, checks the file against its template, shows the changes it proposes, and records what it changed. Next update due 2027-10-01. Open the Tours button for a guided walk-through.

  1. 1
    Load the adopted land use export after the general plan changes. Land use layer
    A parcel export with adopted land use and development status. The build-out sum re-runs; the unit factors stay.
    Effect: re-runs the build-out demand by zone and moves the expansion triggers.

    Edit mode is off

  2. 2
    Add the year's maximum-day production from SCADA. This year's maximum day
    One row per year: date and maximum day in mgd. The tracker moves; the projection does not.
    Effect: updates the phase trigger tracker.

    Edit mode is off

  3. 3
    Import each bid tab through the wizard, after each bid or once a year. Bid tabs
    An Excel bid tab. The wizard matches each line to a standard item and saves the matches per bidder.
    Effect: updates the unit costs and re-prices every project that uses them.

    Edit mode is off

  4. 4
    Load the result tables from the latest model run. Model result tables
    WSC runs the model and sends the zone result tables. The screen shows the run date. No other screen changes the model results.
    Effect: replaces the model results and their run date.

    Edit mode is off

  5. 5
    Review the proposed changes and the act, watch or defer list on the Plan screen.
    A project that moved more than the threshold is flagged there.
  6. 6
    Save a snapshot and set the next due date.
    The snapshot fixes what this update changed. The due date drives the reminder on the Plan screen.

    Edit mode is off Set the due date

User guide

Getting started

What this tool is

Welcome to this limited version of WSC's fully functional mock-up, which walks through some of the functionality that WSC can build into your agency's production toolset. The purpose of this tool is to let staff track demand, time the next expansion, and keep CIP costs current from one place. WSC can build varying levels of tools that are designed to give your agency the most value while right-sizing the deliverable to fit within your technical ecosystem. Deliverables can range from a single self-contained HTML file that runs in your browser to installable programs that interface directly with the other products you already use.

For all but the most limited deliverable options, your staff will be able to load direct exports from third-party tools through the Update tab simulated here. This includes demands, expansion triggers, project costs, bid tabs, and the CIP updates that follow from them. The version you are looking at keeps the whole master plan in one file that opens in any browser, so it carries the build-out demand, the expansion triggers, the model results, and the unit costs from your agency's bids. The same file carries the CIP, a fact sheet for every project, the decision log, and the map with its basemap built in, which means nothing needs to be installed and the file fetches nothing from the network. The plan's data is kept in a data file beside this page rather than in the browser, so several staff can work from the same plan. The master file is shared on the network, where it opens read only until the editor password opens it for editing during a session.

The screens

ScreenWhat it answers
Plan OverviewThis screen tells you what needs a decision this year, where the next expansion trigger falls, what the CIP totals are, what has changed since the snapshot, and when the next update is due.
DemandThis screen shows the build-out demand by zone, the expansion triggers plotted against capacity, and the model results for each planning year.
MapThis screen shows results by parcel and by main, so you can click a facility or a main to see the projects recommended for it.
ProjectsThis screen holds the CIP by fiscal year with the fund target, every project's record and fact sheet, the decision log, and the later-phase upsizing screen.
CostsThis screen shows the unit costs from your agency's bids, the assemblies, and every project re-priced from them, with the bid tabs as the drill-down.
UpdateThis screen carries the annual checklist, the checks behind each import, and the record of every change made to the plan.

The top bar

  • Growth case, horizon, and cost year appear on the screens that use them, and a choice made on one screen applies everywhere in the tool.
  • Edit turns on editing for this session once you enter the editor password, which means that outside Edit mode every screen stays read only.
  • How this is built opens the method cards, which explain the unit factors, the bid crosswalk, the assemblies, and the markups behind every figure.
  • Guide opens this guide at the section for the screen you are on, and Tours lists the guided walk-throughs that are available for that screen.
  • The gear opens Settings, where you can choose your preferences, point the tool at a data file, and set the plan-wide values.
Tip. point at a figure, a column heading, or a control to see what it means, and on a phone you can tap it instead.

Three things to know

  1. The plan adapts to new information, so a new bid re-prices every project that uses the items it priced. In the same way, a new land use layer re-runs build-out and moves the triggers, and a year's maximum day moves the tracker.
  2. Model results are the one thing the file cannot recompute, which means they change only when WSC re-runs the model and the result tables are loaded on the Update screen.
  3. Every change is logged with its date and author, so you can review each update for accuracy before relying on it in a decision or a budget.

Plan Overview screen

Goal

The purpose of this screen is to answer the questions a manager asks first, on one screen, so you can see what needs attention this year without opening the rest of the tool.

What is on it

  • Update reminder. This card shows the due date of the next annual update, and the banner turns amber 60 days before that date and red once it has passed. "Add to calendar" downloads a reminder that you can drop into Outlook.
  • Data file. This card tells you which file you are working in, when it was last saved, and by whom. Because the master is shared on the network, you can check the folder for a newer copy before relying on a figure.
  • Act, watch, or defer. This list places every project using the thresholds set under Settings, where act means the decision is due within the act threshold. Watch means the decision is due within the watch threshold, or that the cost has moved more than the cost threshold since the snapshot, and you can click any project to open its record.
  • Next expansion trigger. This card shows the next capacity step with its trigger demand, the trigger year, and the decision date, and the growth case you choose moves all of them.
  • CIP totals. This card gives the five, 10, and 40 year totals, along with the split between expansion and renewal so you can see where the money goes.
  • Changes since the last snapshot. This card lists the latest entries in the change record, so you can see at a glance what has moved since the plan was last fixed.
  • Open decisions. This card lists the decisions in the log that still need a sign-off, so nothing waits unnoticed.
  • Figures at a glance. This strip shows a tile from every screen, and clicking a tile opens that screen.

How to use it

  1. Read the act list first, because those projects need work this year and the rest of the screen supports that decision.
  2. Check the next trigger against the latest maximum day, so you can see how many years remain before the next capacity step has to be decided.
  3. If the banner is amber or red, open the Update screen and work down the checklist before relying on any figure on this screen.

Demand screen

Goal

The purpose of this screen is to show how much water the system needs at build-out, when each capacity step is needed, and what the model says about each planning year. Together these let you time the next expansion with confidence.

Build-out demand

Build-out demand is summed from parcels, where each parcel carries its adopted land use and a unit demand factor derived from your agency's meter data. The growth case only phases the total in time, which means the build-out ceiling does not change when you switch the case. The chart compares the phased total with the adopted projection so you can see where they diverge.

The horizon and the growth case both come from the strip at the top of the screen, and the same choice applies on every other screen that uses them.

Expansion triggers

Each expansion trigger marks the maximum day demand at which the next capacity step is needed, so you can see how many years remain before a decision has to be made. The chart draws the projected maximum day with its band, the recorded maximum days from SCADA, and each cumulative capacity step. The year where the projection crosses a step is the trigger year. The decision date is the trigger year less the lead time needed for design, permits, and construction.

  • The alternative plant option switch shows how a different way of adding capacity moves the later steps, so you can compare two expansion paths on the same chart.
  • The tracker shows how close the latest recorded maximum day is to the next trigger, which gives you an early reading on whether the projection is holding.
  • The maximum day curve is the build-out demand times the peaking factor, so a land use update moves the triggers without any further input.

Model results

The table shows each zone's minimum pressure, fire flow, water age, and storage for the chosen planning year, and it tells you whether each one meets the criteria. The projects that were switched on in that model run are listed beside the table so you can see what the results assume.

Note. model results are read only, because they change only when WSC re-runs the model and its result tables are loaded on the Update screen, and the run date is shown above the table.

Map screen

Goal

The purpose of this screen is to let you confirm that you are looking at the right asset and the right project before deciding anything, with the results drawn on your agency's own network.

What is on it

  • Color by draws the parcels by zone, land use, or demand, or draws the mains by diameter, so you can read the pattern behind a figure.
  • Layers shows everything at once, hides the projects, or shows the parcels only, which keeps the map readable when you are focused on one question.
  • Pins mark every facility and every main that a project touches, and clicking a pin shows the asset's record and its recommended projects on the right. From there you can click a project to open its record on the Projects screen.

The basemap is built into the file, which means the map works without a web service and without a network connection.

Note. this mock-up shows pictures of invented layers over a public basemap, whereas the delivered file draws your agency's own layers on its own basemap, embedded in the file.

Projects screen

Goal

The purpose of this screen is to hold every project once, with its reason, its cost, its timing, and its stage, so that the CIP, the fact sheets, and the map all read from the same record.

The CIP

  • List switches between expansion, renewal and replacement, or both, and the horizon strip adds the later projects to the earlier ones so you can see the full program.
  • Cost by fiscal year shows the next five years against the fund target, where the dashed line is the cut line and the years over it are named under the chart. In Edit mode, "set" lets you change the targets.
  • The table carries the purpose, trigger, year, stage, zone, who pays, growth share, the connection charge id, the estimate class, and the cost. Where a project was re-priced from the bids, the issued cost is shown under the new one so you can see the move.
  • Click a row to open the project record, which explains why the project is in the plan, the trigger behind its timing, the area served, who pays, its assets, its decisions, and its history.

Editing a project

  1. Turn on Edit mode in the top bar, which asks for the editor password the first time in a session.
  2. Open the project record and choose "Edit project" to bring up the fields you can change.
  3. Change the name, purpose, trigger, area served, planned year, who pays, growth share, or assets, or enter a cost override, and leave the override blank if you want to keep the re-priced cost.
  4. Save the record, and the change is logged with your name while the fact sheet, the map, and the Plan Overview screen show it at once.

"Change stage" moves the project through the workflow from draft to proposed, staff-approved, Board-adopted, deferred, or complete, so everyone can see where a project stands.

Fact sheets

Each fact sheet is one page per project built from the same record, where the staff version carries every fact and the public version states the project in plain language while hiding cost detail and asset ids. You can print either version to PDF from the browser for the Board packet.

Decision log

The decision log records every assumption and approval with its date, basis, and owner role, so you can trace why the plan looks the way it does. In Edit mode, "Add decision" records a new one and can tie it to a project.

Upsizing (later phase)

This desktop screen lists the renewal mains that are worth a larger pipe while the trench is open, and each candidate shows the in-kind cost, the upsized cost, the added cost, and who pays for it.

Costs screen

Goal

The purpose of this screen is to price every project from your agency's own bids, in the cost year shown, with the spread of prices visible so you can judge how firm each estimate is.

Unit costs

  • Policy is the rule that turns a set of bid prices into one unit cost, and the default takes the median of the three lowest bidders on each project and then the median across projects.
  • Standard item costs lists every item with its count of projects and bidders, the low, the chosen value, the high, and the spread, while items with no bids yet use a reference price.
  • Cost build-up shows one project's direct cost, contingency, development, and construction services, so you can see how the total was assembled.
  • Re-priced projects compares every project with its issued cost, and a chip marks any project whose cost moved more than 10%.

The cost year comes from the strip at the top, and prices from older bids are escalated to that year by the index named in Settings.

Bid tabs

This tab lists the loaded bid tabs and the prices per standard item, and you can import a bid tab after each bid or batch the year's bids at once.

Importing a bid tab

The wizard walks you through six steps, and each step shows what it found before you move on.

  1. File. Choose the Excel or CSV bid tab you want to load, in the format your agency already produces.
  2. Columns. Confirm which column is the item number, description, unit, quantity, and each bidder's price. A layout seen before is applied for you, and a new one is saved per bidder when you accept it.
  3. Match items. Each bid line gets a suggested standard item, taking a saved match for this bidder first and then the parser's suggestion from the size, material, and unit. You can change any match from the list, exclude a line, or leave it for the review queue.
  4. Classify the rest. Lines that are not per unit of pipe are spread into the cost per foot of main, so mobilization, bonds, and traffic control become a share of the measured subtotal. Valves, services, fittings, and appurtenances become allowances per foot, and design and construction services become soft-cost percentages.
  5. Review. This step shows the prices per standard item escalated to the cost year, and the projects that will re-price once you accept.
  6. Accept. The tables update, the projects re-price, and the import is logged with your name and the date.
Tip. "How this is built" in the top bar shows the crosswalk table, the review queue, and the saved matches behind the wizard.

Update screen

Goal

The purpose of this screen is to keep the plan current with the exports your agency already produces, once a year or whenever a new bid or land use plan arrives, with every change checked and recorded.

The annual checklist

Work down the numbered steps, where each step says what to load, checks the file against its template, shows the changes it proposes, and records what it changed and who loaded it. A step that has already run shows a green number and its last result, so you can see where you left off.

StepWhat to loadWhat changes
Land use layerLoad the adopted land use export after the general plan changes, in the format your GIS already produces.This step recomputes the build-out demand by zone and moves the expansion triggers to match.
This year's maximum dayLoad one row from SCADA that carries the date and the maximum day in mgd.This step moves the phase trigger tracker so you can see how close the system is to the next step.
Bid tabsLoad each bid tab through the wizard, either one at a time or as a batch for the year.This step updates the unit costs and re-prices every project that uses the items priced.
Project listLoad the finance project list as the export your finance system already produces.This step updates the project timing and cost wherever a row matches a project in the plan.
Model result tablesLoad the zone tables from the latest model run, which WSC sends after each run.This step replaces the model results and records their run date above the table.

Once the steps are done, review the act, watch, or defer list on the Plan Overview screen, save a snapshot, and set the next due date so the reminder stays accurate.

Note. a file that fails a template check is listed with the rows that failed, so you can fix the export and load it again without losing anything, and no failure is hidden from you.

QA/QC summary

This panel shows the checks behind the figures, including how many imports passed, the bid items still to review, and the projects that moved more than 10%. It also counts the changes since the snapshot and the draft projects, and it runs a self-check that the totals re-sum to the project list.

Change record

The change record lists every change in the file with its date, author, what it changed, and the value before and after, and you can export it as CSV for a review.

Snapshots and exports

A snapshot fixes the plan at a point in time along with its stage, and from here you can export the data file, a dated HTML copy, or the next five fiscal years in the budget template columns.

Settings and files

Preferences

Preferences cover the theme, the default growth case and horizon, and whether the method cards show, and they are kept on this computer so they need no password.

Data files

The plan's data is kept in a data file beside this page rather than in the browser, which means several staff can use the same plan at once.

  • Master file. The master is the shared file on the network, and it opens read only until the editor password opens it for editing during a session. You choose it once, and the tool remembers it on this computer.
  • Personal file. Your personal file holds your own scenarios and draft projects, and you choose "personal" under "Working in" to use it. A scenario or project can be copied into the master with the editor password.
  • Before relying on a figure, check the network folder for a newer master, because the Plan Overview screen shows when the file was saved and by whom.

There are other ways to control who edits the master, and WSC can set either of them up with your agency's IT at scoping:

  1. IT can place the master in a folder where only editors have write permission, which means no password is needed at all.
  2. A hosted version can use your agency's Microsoft sign-in and roles, so access follows the accounts you already manage.

Plan settings

These settings need Edit mode, because they change figures across the whole plan.

  • Cost year defaults to the current year, Escalation index names the index used to bring older bid prices up to it, and Year of expenditure escalates each project to its planned year.
  • Act, watch, or defer thresholds set the years and the cost change that place each project in one of the three lists on the Plan Overview screen.
  • Steward, due date, and fiscal year drive the reminder, the banner, and the fiscal-year columns, so they should be set when the plan is first issued.
  • Editor password keeps casual edits out of the master, but it is not security, because the file is readable by anyone with access to the folder.

How data gets in

By delivery level

LevelHow a newer figure reaches the file
WSC-issued fileWSC loads the exports and reissues the file at each milestone, so your staff read the current issue without loading anything themselves.
Staff-updated fileYour staff load the exports on the Update screen, where the file checks each one against its template, recomputes, and logs every change.

By feed

FeedWhere it comes fromHow it gets inWhat changes when it is loaded
Land use and parcelsThe feed is the county parcel layer with adopted land use, exported from your GIS.You load a GIS export on the Update screen, or at the connected level the refresher pulls it from the feature service.Loading it recomputes the build-out demand by zone and moves the expansion triggers.
Maximum dayThe feed is the SCADA historian that already records your daily production.You type or export one row a year, or at the connected level the refresher pulls it from the historian.Loading it moves the phase trigger tracker to the latest recorded maximum day, so you can see how close the system is to the next step.
Bid tabsThe feed is your agency's bid tabulations in Excel, in the layout each bidder already uses.You load each tab through the wizard, or at the connected level a watched bid folder feeds them in.Loading it updates the unit costs and re-prices every project that uses the items priced.
Project listThe feed is the finance project list that your finance staff already maintain.You load the export on the Update screen and the tool matches each row to a project.Loading it updates the project timing and cost wherever a row matches a project already in the plan.
Model resultsThe feed is the hydraulic model, which WSC runs when the project set changes.You load the zone result tables on the Update screen after WSC sends them.Loading it replaces the model results on the Demand screen and records their run date above the table.
GIS layersThe feed is your agency's mains, facilities, and parcels as maintained in your GIS.WSC rebuilds the layers at each issue, or at the connected level the refresher rebuilds them on its schedule.Loading it redraws the map and refreshes the asset records behind each pin.
Decisions and project editsThe feed is your own staff, working in Edit mode with the editor password.You type decisions and project edits straight into the tool, and each one is logged with your name.Entering them updates the decision log and the project records that the CIP and fact sheets read.

What the file never does

  • The file never connects to the model, the CMMS, or SCADA on its own, which means changes in those systems reach the file only when an export is loaded.
  • The file never changes a model result, because a different set of projects needs a fresh model run before the results can change.
  • The file never changes a unit factor, since new factors come with a master plan update rather than with an annual refresh.

Troubleshooting

What you seeWhat to do
A control is greyed with "Edit mode is off"Click the control, or the Edit button in the top bar, and enter the editor password to turn on editing for this session.
A control is greyed with "available from"The feature belongs to a higher delivery level than this file, so it is shown here to illustrate what WSC can build rather than to be used.
The banner says the update is overdueOpen the Update screen and work down the checklist, then set the next due date under Settings so the banner clears.
An import failed a template checkThe rows that failed are listed for you, so you can fix the export against the template named and load it again.
A project's cost does not match the issued costThe project was re-priced from a newer bid, so the issued cost is shown under the new one and the change record says which import moved it.
The master file is read onlyThis is normal, because the master opens read only for everyone and the editor password opens it for editing during a session.
Someone else saved the master after you opened itThe tool compares the saved time before it writes and shows you the other author's changes, so you can reload or merge before saving.
The file asks for the data file againThe browser has forgotten the file handle on this computer, so choose the same master file again and you will find that none of your work has been lost.
The page shows a blank screen on a phoneThe iPhone Files preview runs no scripts, so open the file in Safari or a browser app to see the full tool.

Terms

Every term below also shows as a tip when you point at it in the tool.

TermMeaning
actThe decision on this project is due within the act threshold (Settings). Start the work that leads to the decision.
act watch deferEach project's recommendation. Act: the decision is due within the act threshold. Watch: due within the watch threshold, or the cost moved more than the cost threshold since the snapshot. Defer: beyond both. The thresholds are set under Settings.
added costThe cost of the larger pipe less the cost of replacing in kind.
alt optionAn alternative way to add capacity. Turning it on shows how it moves the timing of the next step.
annual updateThe yearly checklist on the Update screen: load the year's exports, review the proposed changes, save a snapshot.
assemblyThe cost per unit of a whole piece of work: a foot of main with its trench, paving, valves and services; a million gallons of tank; a million gallons a day of pumping or treatment.
average dayAnnual water demand divided by 365 days.
bid tabA bid tabulation: the unit prices every bidder offered on one project, line by line.
buildoutThe demand when every parcel is developed to its adopted land use. Summed from parcels and unit factors, not projected from a growth rate.
capacity stepOne phase of plant or facility capacity. Steps add up; the chart shows the cumulative capacity after each.
change recordEvery change in the file: when, who, what, from and to. It travels with the data file.
cipThe capital improvement program: every project with its purpose, trigger, cost, timing, area served and who pays.
cost buildupDirect cost, then contingency by estimate class, then project development and construction services, add up to the total.
cost yearThe dollar year every cost is shown in. Prices from older bids are escalated to it by the index named in Settings. It defaults to the current year.
crosswalkThe saved match between a bidder's description and a standard item. Reused on the next bid tab from that bidder.
decision dateThe trigger year less the lead time for design, permits and construction. The decision to proceed is needed by this year.
decision logThe dated record of planning decisions, their basis and the role that owns them.
deferThe decision on this project falls beyond the watch threshold, so no action is needed this year.
due dateWhen the next annual update is due. The banner turns amber 60 days before and red after. Add it to your calendar with the button.
edit modeUnlocks editing for this session after the editor password. Every edit is logged with your name.
estimate classHow firm the cost is. Class 5 is a planning-level estimate with a wide range; class 4 is narrower. The range is shown on the fact sheet.
fire flowWhether the zone delivers the required fire flow at the required residual pressure.
fiscal yearThe agency's budget year, set under Settings.
fund targetThe amount each fund can spend in a fiscal year. The cut line in the chart marks it; projects above it move or defer.
growth caseHow fast build-out is reached: low, base or high. Build-out itself does not change with the case.
growth shareThe share of a project's cost that serves growth and is charged to expansion.
guideThe user guide, opened at the section for this screen.
horizonHow far ahead the screen looks: 5, 10 or 40 years, or build-out. A longer horizon adds the later projects to the earlier ones.
how builtShows the method behind each screen: unit factors, the bid crosswalk, the assemblies and the markups.
in kindReplacement at the same size and material.
layersWhich layers the map draws. Pins mark facilities and the mains a project touches.
master fileThe shared data file on the network. It opens read only; the editor password unlocks it. A personal file holds your own scenarios.
maximum dayThe highest one-day demand in a year. Capacity is planned to it. Maximum day is average day times the peaking factor.
min pressureThe lowest pressure in the zone under the run's conditions, against the agency's service criterion.
model resultsFigures from the hydraulic model. They change only when the model is re-run and its result tables are loaded on the Update screen.
parcelOne lot in the county parcel layer, with its adopted land use and development status.
planning yearThe year a model run represents, with the projects switched on in that run.
policyThe rule that turns a set of bid prices into one unit cost, such as the median of the three lowest bidders.
qaqcThe checks behind the figures: template checks on every import, the bid items still to review, projects that moved more than 10 percent, and a self-check that the totals re-sum.
quantity effectA flag that a larger quantity won a lower unit price, so the price depends on the size of the job.
repricedA project cost recomputed from the current unit cost table, compared with the issued cost.
review queueBid lines that have no confirmed match yet. They do not price anything until matched.
snapshotA fixed point in the plan with its stage and date. Changes after it are listed on the Plan screen.
spreadThe low to high range of the prices behind a unit cost, with the chosen value marked.
stageWhere a project sits in the approval workflow: draft, proposed, staff-approved, Board-adopted, deferred or complete.
standard itemOne line of the standard cost list, such as an 8-inch open-cut PVC main with concrete encasement, per foot. Every bid line is matched to one.
stewardThe person who keeps the plan current and runs the annual update. Named at scoping.
toursGuided walk-throughs of the larger workflows on this screen. A tour runs on a throwaway copy and changes nothing.
trackerHow close the latest recorded maximum day is to the next trigger.
triggerThe maximum-day demand at which a capacity step is needed. The trigger year is the year the projected maximum day reaches it.
upsizingReplacing a main at a larger size while the trench is open, where build-out needs the capacity.
watchThis project is inside the watch threshold, or its cost moved more than the cost threshold since the snapshot. Check it at the next update.
water ageHow long water sits in the system before use. Long ages point to water quality risk.
who paysExpansion projects are paid by new development through the connection charge. Renewal and replacement is paid by existing customers. A split project carries a growth share.
year of expenditureA cost escalated from the cost year to the year the project is built.
zoneA pressure zone: the area served from one hydraulic grade.
